---
title: "A-optimality"
description: "A-optimality minimizes the average variance of the ridge coefficients."
---

A-optimality minimizes the average variance of the ridge coefficients. It uses the training set alone.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Optimal design |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | no (a test set given to `optTrain()` is ignored) |
| Score a given set | `aopt_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "AOpt")` |

## Definition

With $\lambda = 1/p$: $\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{tr}[(X'X + \lambda I)^{-1}]$. Akdemir and Isidro-Sánchez (2019) allow a contrast matrix; TSDFGS uses the identity. For $p > n$ the $p - n$ zero eigenvalues each add $1/\lambda$.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
aopt_score(geno[1:50, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "AOpt",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Akdemir, D., & Isidro-Sánchez, J. (2019). Design of training populations for selective phenotyping in genomic prediction. *Scientific Reports, 9*, 1446. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-38081-6>

Akdemir, D., Sanchez, J. I., & Jannink, J.-L. (2015). Optimization of genomic selection training populations with a genetic algorithm. *Genetics Selection Evolution, 47*, 38. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12711-015-0116-6>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package STPGA by Akdemir and colleagues: [CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA) (GPL-3).

## License review

Formulas and algorithms are ideas and methods, which copyright does not protect. Where an original package is under a GPL license, we read it to check our results and credit it; TSDFGS is [GPL-3](https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS/blob/main/LICENSE.md), which is compatible with GPL-3 and GPL (>= 3) code. This is our reading of the public record, not legal advice; see the [license review](criteria-license-review.html).

* **Original software:** STPGA, GPL-3 (AOPT); compared, not copied. STPGA reports the trace divided by $p$, which does not change the optimum.
* **Article license:** Akdemir and Isidro-Sánchez (2019) open access (Scientific Reports).
* **Verdict:** included.
